name: round
does: Rounds a number to a given number of decimal places.
note: Halves round to the nearest even number, so `round(0.5)` is 0 and `round(1.5)` is 2.

name: class
does: Tells you what type of value something is — numeric, character, logical. The first thing to check when a function gives you something odd.

name: log
does: Calculates a logarithm.
note: The default base is *e*, about 2.718 — not 10. `log(100)` is about 4.61.

name: paste
does: Joins values together into one piece of text.

name: c
does: Combines several values into one vector. Short for combine.
note: A vector holds one type only. If any value is text, every value becomes text.

name: length
does: Counts how many values there are.

name: sum
does: Adds up numbers. On TRUE and FALSE, counts how many are TRUE.

name: mean
does: The average. On TRUE and FALSE, gives the fraction that are TRUE.
note: Needs numbers. On text it warns and returns `NA`.

name: max
does: The largest value.

name: sort
does: Puts values in order, lowest first unless told otherwise.

name: as.numeric
does: Converts text into numbers.
note: Anything that can't be read as a number becomes `NA`, with a warning.

name: is.na
does: Finds missing values. Gives TRUE for each missing value and FALSE for everything else. The only reliable way to ask what's missing — `== NA` does not work.
note: Count missing values with `sum(is.na(x))`, and drop them with `x[!is.na(x)]`.

name: data.frame
does: Builds a table from vectors of the same length. Each vector becomes a column, and each position becomes a row.
note: Every column must be the same length — one value per row. Otherwise it stops with an error.

name: str
does: Shows the structure of a data frame — how many rows and columns, and the type of every column. The quickest way to spot a number that's secretly text.
result:
'data.frame':	2 obs. of  2 variables:
 $ age: num  67 54
 $ sbp: chr  "142" "118"
note: In a spreadsheet-style view, `142` and `"142"` look identical. `str()` shows the difference — `num` versus `chr`.

name: summary
does: A quick overview — smallest, largest, middle, average, and how many values are missing. On a whole data frame, it does every column at once.
result:
Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.    NA's
  118.0   124.5   131.0   135.0   143.5   156.0       1

name: nrow
does: Counts the rows in a data frame — how many patients, how many observations.
note: After filtering, a count that looks one too high is worth a second look — an `NA` in the filter can add a row of `NA`s.

name: ifelse
does: Gives one of two values, depending on a question. For each value, `yes` if the test is TRUE, `no` if it's FALSE.
note: The order is test, then yes, then no. Naming them — `test =`, `yes =`, `no =` — stops the labels ending up backwards.

name: names
does: Lists the names of the pieces inside something — the parts of a list, or the columns of a data frame. The quickest way to see what's in a result you don't recognise.

name: t.test
usage: t.test(x, y, var.equal = FALSE, paired = FALSE, ...)
does: Compares the means of two groups. Gives back a list you can take the p-value, interval and means out of with `$`.
note: Runs Welch's test unless you set `var.equal = TRUE`. The first two arguments are labelled `x` and `y` in the printout, not by your names. Missing values are dropped without a word.

name: print
does: Shows a value. Outside a loop R shows results for you; inside a loop, nothing appears unless something prints it.

name: sqrt
does: Square root.
